thread:
taylor: hey all — opened PR #2040 that adjusts KV cache TTL and adds an adaptive-evict path to reduce memory during cold tails. perf/load notes in the PR description. can someone take a quick look? trying to get this into today's merge window (17:00 UTC). :hourglass_flowing_sand:

link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2040

rohan: taking a peek now. quick Q — does this change the cache key format at all? we need to ensure downstream routing still matches the shard mapping.

kevin: I glanced at the patch. no key format change, just TTL + eviction heuristics. ran a 10m soak at 2k QPS on a staging rig: throughput +3.5%, avg token latency unchanged, p95 up ~6ms. logs looked clean.

maya: thanks kevin. can you paste the perf script/command you used? want to reproduce with quantized model profiles (int8) — evictions might interact with KV cache hits.

kevin: sure — command I used:

```
# simple wrk-like load
./bench --region=us-west --concurrency=64 --qps=2000 --duration=600 --model=redwood-7b-quant4
```

and the tail snapshot: `p50 18ms, p95 62ms, p99 140ms`

nina: CI bot shows one flaky test in `cache_integration_test::evict_policy_race`, failing intermittently. CI log: `AssertionError: expected hit_ratio > 0.7 but got 0.68` — might be test sensitivity to timing. cc @taylor

ci-bot: build #4269 · runtime · PR #2040 — tests: 118 passed, 1 flaky failed. See pipeline: https://ci.redwood-inference/internal/4269

taylor: noted — i'll add a small timing slack in the test and re-run. the change includes a new config knob `adaptive_evict.window_ms` (default 200). intended behavior: when tail tokens spike, we momentarily lower TTL to free slots for hot prefixes. config snippet in PR:

```
cache:
  default_ttl_ms: 300000
  adaptive_evict:
    enabled: true
    window_ms: 200
    min_ttl_ms: 1000
```

rohan: does turning on adaptive_evict require any routing policy changes? e.g., should we prefer `low-latency` route for inference that benefits from longer TTL?

kevin: routing unaffected, but we saw in canary that models with high prefix reuse benefited more. for mixed workloads (many short unique prompts) memory drop was ~12% which cuts cost.

maya: one more thought — quantized kernels can increase per-batch compute density, so the eviction cadence might need to be slightly higher to avoid OOM in tight GPU memory scenarios. can we add a per-model override?

taylor: good call. PR adds `cache.per_model_overrides` so ops can tune TTL per model. example in PR.

nina: re-run CI after test tweak, then we should be able to merge if we get one more approval. can someone from eng-runtime owners + perf please approve? i'm on standby to promote the canary after merge.

kevin: approved. :thumbsup:

rohan: left a small comment about docstrings, but not blocking. approved from my side too. :eyes:

maya: flagged one nit on naming; otherwise LGTM. approved.

ci-bot: PR #2040 — all required approvals present. merge target: next merge window at 17:00 UTC.

taylor: thanks folks — i'll push the test fix now and request the merge lock. planning a short canary (30m) on a single dedicated pool, will monitor p95 and cost delta. ping here when promoting. :rocket:
